end.summary:
Food miles was introduced as the distance food travels from farm to plate.
Rohan identified nearby spinach and Shimla apples as examples of different travel distances.
They practised links between longer distances, fuel use, pollution, freshness, refrigeration, and packaging.
Rohan’s teach-back was not yet complete; they did not independently answer all effect questions.
end.parentNote: Asha practised defining food miles and comparing nearby and far-travelled foods with Rohan. They gave a clear example using spinach from nearby fields and apples from Shimla, and identified pollution, fuel use, and reduced freshness as effects. Rohan initially mixed up whether farther-travelled food is better and needed prompts for some effects; this was partly corrected later when they explained the definition and named pollution and freshness. At home, ask them to compare two foods and say which travelled farther, then name one effect on fuel, pollution, or freshness.
